name: Pembrolizumab (cutaneous melanoma)

biomarkers.note: Anti-PD-1 monotherapy. No positive companion biomarker is required to start; applicable regardless of BRAF status. Used in the adjuvant setting for resected high-risk stage III (KEYNOTE-054) and in the unresectable/metastatic setting (KEYNOTE-002, KEYNOTE-006). Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Melanoma: Cutaneous, Table 14.

lineOfTherapy: adjuvant anti-PD-1 for resected high-risk stage III melanoma, and single-agent anti-PD-1 for unresectable stage III or stage IV melanoma; not BRAF-restricted

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: resected high-risk stage III (adjuvant) OR unresectable stage III / stage IV (advanced)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Pembrolizumab as adjuvant and advanced-disease anti-PD-1 option; Table 14, MS-56

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab

provenance.locator: Table 14 Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Treatment Regimens, Pembrolizumab row, MS-56 (line 8170): FDA Prescribing information 200 mg Q3W; KEYNOTE-002 (line 8164) 2 mg/kg Q3W

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Table 14 (MS-56). Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV flat every 3 weeks (FDA prescribing information), until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Source-stated weight-based alternative: 2 mg/kg Q3W (KEYNOTE-002, line 8164); the higher 10 mg/kg Q3W/Q2W trial arms (KEYNOTE-002/006) showed no benefit over the standard dose and are not modeled. In the adjuvant setting pembrolizumab 200 mg Q3W is given for up to 1 year; in advanced disease it is continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity (see regimen.cycles).

regimen.cycles: Adjuvant (resected stage III): pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for up to 1 year (approximately 17 cycles). Advanced (unresectable stage III / stage IV): pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Table 14, MS-56). A 400 mg every-6-weeks flat schedule is an accepted labeling alternative but is not printed in the melanoma table and is not modeled.
supportiveCare: Immune-related adverse event (irAE) monitoring (thyroid and other endocrinopathies, hepatitis, colitis/diarrhea, pneumonitis, dermatitis, nephritis); manage per NCCN Guidelines for Management of Immunotherapy-Related Toxicities.
Baseline and periodic thyroid (TSH/free T4), liver function, glucose as indicated.

monitoring: immune-related toxicity screen (TSH/free T4, LFTs, glucose) before each cycle and as indicated
symptom review for colitis, pneumonitis, dermatitis, endocrinopathy
clinical/radiographic response assessment (advanced disease); recurrence surveillance (adjuvant)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold pembrolizumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; permanent discontinuation for severe/grade 3 to 4 irAE. Obtain clinical review before rechallenge.

core.locator: Anti-PD-1 monotherapy framework for melanoma; dosing taken from the guideline layer (Table 14, MS-56)

guideline.locator: Table 14 Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Treatment Regimens, Pembrolizumab (FDA prescribing information 200 mg Q3W; KEYNOTE-002 2 mg/kg Q3W), MS-56 (lines 8162 to 8171)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for pembrolizumab anti-PD-1 monotherapy in cutaneous melanoma, covering both adjuvant therapy for resected high-risk stage III disease and treatment of unresectable stage III or stage IV disease. The dose is sourced to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Melanoma: Cutaneous v2.2026, Table 14 (MS-56): pembrolizumab 200 mg IV flat every 3 weeks (FDA prescribing information), with a source-stated weight-based alternative of 2 mg/kg every 3 weeks (KEYNOTE-002). Adjuvant duration is up to 1 year; advanced-disease treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Immune-related adverse event monitoring applies. Every modeled numeric dose is sourced and no field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
